solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Backward-looking archbishop is issue for TV announcement

indicators.note: looking backward tells us to read the whole string of pieces from right to left

parts.note: Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury in the 1930s, a crossword regular
to issue is to emit or send out

explanation.surface: A cleric with nostalgic views makes a statement for broadcast television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward-looking' turns LANG + IS + EMIT, giving LANGISEMIT read from the right.
explanation.definitionFit: The pips broadcast on the hour are a kind of announcement telling viewers or listeners the exact time.

clue.text: Food — one who looked overfed?

definitions.meaning: Friar ..., Robin Hood's companion, is traditionally a portly, well-fed monk

explanation.surface: A question about eating and someone who seemed to have eaten too much.
explanation.definitionFit: British schoolchildren call snacks tuck, and the Robin Hood legend's jolly friar bears the name and a large belly.

clue.text: Feel astonishment meeting line produced by poet

parts.note: to marvel is to be filled with wonder

explanation.surface: Wonder at a line of verse written by a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Marvell was the 17th-century English metaphysical poet of 'To His Coy Mistress'.

clue.text: Well as he'd done, it's out of order to be conceited

indicators.note: something out of order is jumbled up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Boasting about how well you did is improper and vain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' looks like a judgment on bad behaviour, but it is the anagram signal for WELL AS HE'D DONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a big head in the idiomatic sense is vain and has far too high an opinion of themselves.

clue.text: Author with endless dynamism about to pen end of tale

indicators.note: to pen something is to enclose it, so one piece goes inside another
about here means turned around, so the letters are read backwards
without its end, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: dynamism is drive or energy

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A novelist, short of drive, writes the last part of a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims ENERGY to ENERG, 'about' turns it to GRENE, and 'to pen' puts E, the last letter of 'tale', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was the English novelist of 'Brighton Rock' and 'The Power and the Glory'.

clue.text: Rider in habit, not cold

indicators.note: not here means the following piece is left out of the word

parts.note: an addiction is a compulsive habit
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A horseman wearing riding clothes, which aren't warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' looks like a horseman and 'habit' like riding dress; 'not' removes C from ADDICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an extra clause tacked onto a document or bill, something supplementary appended.

clue.text: Publisher wants opening chapter to be a stunning success

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: OUP is Oxford University Press

explanation.surface: A publishing house hopes its first chapter will be a smash hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a brilliant, unexpected triumph or masterstroke.

clue.text: I start to grimace a lot — a nasty sort of pain

indicators.note: something nasty is twisted or unpleasant, so these letters are mixed up
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone describes pulling faces constantly because of a horrid ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' scrambles I, G (the first letter of 'grimace'), A LOT and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Otalgia is the medical term for earache, a specific kind of ache.

clue.text: Inferior writers presenting author with samples

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
tasters are small samples offered to try

explanation.surface: Bad scribblers are given a famous writer and some extracts to study.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetaster is a writer of trivial or bad verse, a would-be poet.

clue.text: Old king keeping dry for the most part in carriage

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: arid means dry

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch stays mostly dry while riding in his coach.
explanation.walkthrough: The monarch is the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme; 'keeping' wraps him around the shortened dry word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cariole is a small light horse-drawn carriage, or a Canadian sled.

clue.text: Let down after US agent returned behind schedule

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a Fed is an FBI agent in US slang
late means behind time

explanation.surface: Disappointed after an American agent came back later than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: To let down a tyre or balloon is to let the air out of it; it also means to humble someone.

clue.text: Philosopher loud with obsequiousness when meeting bunch of celebrities

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
unction is an oily, fawning manner
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A thinker fawns loudly when meeting a crowd of famous people.
explanation.definitionFit: A functionalist holds the philosophical view that mental states are defined by their causal roles.

clue.text: PM very familiar with good fashion

parts.note: to be well in with someone is to be on very friendly terms
ton is an old word for high fashion

explanation.surface: A prime minister cosy with stylish people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of Wellington, victor of Waterloo, was later British Prime Minister.

clue.text: Area at end of journey somewhere in India

indicators.note: the area letter is placed after the journey word

parts.note: a go is a turn or trip

explanation.surface: A region reached at the end of a trip through India.
explanation.definitionFit: Goa is a small state on the west coast of India, famous for beaches.

clue.text: Intending to go on to the match?

definitions.text: Intending to go on to the match?

parts.words: Intending to go on to the match?
parts.note: a suitor with ... intentions means to marry, the match being a wedding, not a sporting fixture

explanation.surface: A fan planning to attend the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests football; here it is a marriage match.
explanation.definitionFit: Honourable intentions is the idiom for a suitor's plan to propose and wed.

clue.text: Couple of eggs — potentially boring tea

parts.note: an egg looks like O, so two eggs are OO
something long may be tedious

explanation.surface: Two eggs and a dull cuppa make a dreary breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Oolong is a partly fermented Chinese tea, between green and black.

clue.text: Tighten up legal agreement

explanation.surface: Firm up the terms of a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscles shrink and tighten, while a binding deal enforceable in law has the same spelling as a noun.

clue.text: A wagon with beer brought round, offering a choice

indicators.note: brought round means placed around another piece, enclosing it

parts.note: ale is beer
a cart is a wagon

explanation.surface: A drinks trolley with beer is wheeled round, giving a selection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought round' suggests serving drinks, but it signals the beer enclosing the wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordering from the menu item by item, rather than a set meal, lets diners pick freely.

clue.text: Manoeuvring honestly or sneakily?

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving things around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is someone scheming fairly or underhandedly?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface contrasts honesty with deceit; HONESTLY is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something secretly or covertly is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Your clothes designer brought up something hidden under the neck

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Christian Dior, the French couturier

explanation.surface: Your fashion designer raised a concealed item beneath the collar.
explanation.definitionFit: This gland sits in the front of the throat, out of sight beneath the skin.

clue.text: Sports ground with companies backing game

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground in British usage
COS is the abbreviation for companies

explanation.surface: Firms sponsor a sports ground for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like sponsorship but reverses RECCOS. A rec is a British public recreation ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Association football, the sport, is called this in America and elsewhere.

clue.text: Reduce price of pile in exhibition centre that's mounted up

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
in a down entry, mounted up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the NEC is the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham
a heap is a pile

explanation.surface: Mark down a stack of goods displayed at a trade fair.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Exhibition Centre is a big venue in Birmingham, England; 'that's mounted up' reverses it and 'in' sets the pile inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheapen goods is to lower their cost or value.

clue.text: What's good in Paris — Tuilleries's latest thing, excellent garden feature

parts.note: bon is French for good

indicators.note: the latest letter of a word is its last

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI

explanation.surface: Something good in a Paris park: the newest prized ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: AI stands for A1, top quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai are miniature trees grown in pots, often a feature of Japanese gardens.

clue.text: Bit of scale revealed by fish

definitions.meaning: in tonic sol-fa, the second note of the scale is spelt ... or re
a flat cartilaginous fish such as the skate

explanation.surface: A fish's scale fragment is exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: The note after doh in sol-fa is spelt this way, and it is also the name of a flat sea fish.

clue.text: Degrees needing particular days — be avoiding one month for collection

indicators.note: a collection gathers something in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: dates are particular days

indicators.note: avoiding means leaving out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: October is a month

explanation.surface: Qualifications require set days, steering clear of one month for a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' strips the clue's 'be' out of the month, and 'for collection' has the days gather what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctorates are the highest academic qualifications, such as a PhD.

clue.text: Indian having long passage sealed off at either end

indicators.note: sealing off both ends drops the first and last letters

parts.note: a screed is a long piece of writing

explanation.surface: A Native American finds a lengthy corridor closed at both ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long passage' suggests a corridor but is a lengthy text; 'sealed off at either end' removes S and D.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cree are a First Nations people of Canada, so a Cree is a North American Indian.

clue.text: Left-wing sphere without love set about deep thinker

indicators.note: set about means turned around, so the letters are read in reverse
without in its old sense of outside: the sphere sits outside the love letter

parts.note: red is the colour of the left
love is zero in tennis, O
an orb is a sphere

explanation.surface: A socialist world lacking affection surrounds a pensive person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking but means outside; 'set about' reverses REDOORB.
explanation.definitionFit: One who broods dwells long and deeply on things, a ponderer.

clue.text: Sportsperson digesting very quiet team talk from him?

indicators.note: digesting means taking in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a skier is a sportsperson
PP is pianissimo, very quietly in music

explanation.surface: An athlete quietly absorbing a pep talk delivered by someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: The captain of a side is the one who gives the pre-match pep talk.

clue.text: Remainder to despatch? Put first bit to the back

definitions.note: a singular word for what is left over, defining a plural noun meaning leftovers

indicators.text: Put first bit to the back
indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is moved to its end

parts.note: to despatch is to send

explanation.surface: Instructions for sending off the leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds and ends are the remnants or scraps left over.

clue.text: Possibility for "mint": create money

indicators.note: the arrangement is one possible reordering of these letters

explanation.surface: A mint's chance to make cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A remittance is a sum of money sent in payment.
